minutes.headline: Planning Board approved standard pruning and removal of only eight imminent-threat trees on scenic roads for Unitil.
minutes.summary: The board closed a continued scenic road hearing on Unitil's tree removal and pruning plan after hearing residents and the tree warden. It approved normal pruning and removal of the red-priority trees only, with replacement trees set by the tree warden. It also approved a de minimis Dunkin sign change, took up Butterfly Lane road closeout, the draft earth removal bylaw and the Economic Development Committee charge, and made no recommendation on 250 Howard Street.

public_comment.topic: Opposed aggressive tree removal; described past Unitil clearing on Reservoir Road and urged weighing stormwater.
Asked what work goes beyond the list of trees and asked the town to mark the trees it wants removed.
Questioned the replacement tree offer and said she would rather lose power than lose trees.
Clarified she does not wish power outages on anyone.

Make no recommendation on 250 Howard Street.
Nominate Tanner Cole to the TC Passios building committee.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board approved normal pruning and removal of only eight listed trees on scenic roads for Unitil, with replacements set by the tree warden.
The board closed the public hearing on Unitil's scenic road request after hearing from residents and the tree warden.
The board approved a de minimis change moving the Dunkin menu board at 400 Electric Ave.
The board voted to make no recommendation on the Chapter 61 first refusal for 250 Howard Street, where the town has 120 days to act.
The earth removal bylaw threshold and the Economic Development Committee charge were both put off to the October 7 meeting.

why_it_matters: Scenic road tree removal by the utility is limited to the listed trees, which touches roadside trees, stormwater and how much clearing neighbors will see.

The 250 Howard Street first refusal window is running with no board recommendation, so any decision to buy or pass on the parcel falls to other town bodies and could come to a vote with tax and purchase costs.
Accepting Butterfly Lane as a public road would raise the town's Chapter 90 road funding, so closeout of that road has a small effect on state road aid.
